title: The proposed study employs stakeholder theory as its broad theoretical foundation and stakeholder-salience theory as its middle-range operational lens. Power, legitimacy, and urgency function as sensitizing concepts for examining how organizational actors interpret and prioritize competing recovery claims. The study conceptualizes stakeholder prioritization as operating through decision-rights allocation, escalation pathways, exception authority, and evidence-acceptance practices that collectively shape recoverability assurance. Accordingly, the SAL → DR → ESC → AE relationship is positioned as a proposed, contingency-sensitive conceptual process model rather than an established theory. Through generic qualitative inquiry, critical-incident prompts, reflexive analysis, and interview–artifact triangulation, the study will examine whether empirical evidence supports, refines, extends, complicates, or contradicts the proposed governance-to-assurance mechanism.
